commands.name: ping
commands.desc: Tests reachability with ICMP Echo Request/Echo Reply. Use it first when a host appears down or to confirm a path is working.
commands.sample:
Reply from 192.168.1.1: bytes=32 time=2ms TTL=128
Request timed out.

commands.name: extended ping
commands.desc: Interactive form of ping on a Cisco router/switch; prompts for source address, repeat count, timeout, data size and the destination. Use it to test a specific source interface or to flood a small number of packets.
commands.sample:
Protocol [ip]:
Target IP address: 192.168.10.2
Repeat count [5]: 10
Data size [100]: 1500

commands.name: traceroute
commands.desc: Shows the path a packet takes hop by hop by varying the TTL. Use it to find where along the path a failure happens.

commands.name: tracert
commands.desc: Windows equivalent of traceroute; reveals the route and per-hop latency to a destination.

commands.name: traceroute
commands.desc: Linux equivalent of traceroute; identifies the hops along the path and their response times.

commands.name: ipconfig /all
commands.desc: Displays full TCP/IP configuration: IPv4/IPv6 address, subnet mask, default gateway, MAC address and DHCP server. Use it to verify or troubleshoot addressing on a Windows host.
commands.sample:
Ethernet adapter Ethernet0:
   IPv4 Address. . . . . . . . . . . : 192.168.1.10
   Subnet Mask . . . . . . . . . . . : 255.255.255.0
   Default Gateway . . . . . . . . . : 192.168.1.1

commands.name: ifconfig
commands.desc: Legacy Linux command that shows interface addresses, mask and MAC. Mostly replaced by ip addr but still found on many systems.
commands.sample:
eth0: flags=4163<UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST>  mtu 1500
        inet 192.168.1.10  netmask 255.255.255.0  broadcast 192.168.1.255

commands.name: ip addr
commands.desc: Modern Linux command that shows interface state, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, masks and MAC addresses.
commands.sample:
2: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500
    inet 192.168.1.10/24 brd 192.168.1.255 scope global eth0
    inet6 fe80::a00:27ff:fe11:2233/64 scope link

commands.name: arp -a
commands.desc: Displays the Address Resolution Protocol cache, mapping IPv4 addresses to MAC addresses of neighbors in the LAN. Output format differs slightly by OS (Windows uses hyphenated MACs; Linux prints dotted-quad MACs in brackets).
commands.sample: 192.168.1.1     aa-bb-cc-dd-ee-ff  dynamic

commands.name: show cdp neighbors
commands.desc: Lists directly connected Cisco devices learned via CDP, with device type, interface, and platform. Useful to map the physical topology.
commands.sample:
Device ID    Local Intrfce   Holdtme  Platform
Switch-2     Gig 0/0        122      Cisco 2960

commands.name: show ip interface brief
commands.desc: Shows a quick table of each interface, its IP address, status, and the protocol status. First place to look for down interfaces.
commands.sample:
Interface      IP-Address      OK? Method Status    Protocol
GigabitEthernet0/0  192.168.1.1  YES manual up       up
GigabitEthernet0/1  unassigned      YES unset  down     down

commands.name: show ipv6 interface brief
commands.desc: Lists each interface with its IPv6 address, status, and protocol state. Use it to verify IPv6 configuration and link-local addresses.
commands.sample:
GigabitEthernet0/0    [up/up]
    FE80::200:1FF:FE00:1
    2001:DB8:ACAD:1::1/64

commands.name: show version
commands.desc: Displays the IOS version, uptime, hardware/platform, and the amount of RAM/flash. Use it to confirm the software version and system uptime.
commands.sample:
Cisco IOS Software, C2960 Software (C2960-LANBASEK9-M)
System restarted at 10:00:00 UTC Mon Nov 16 2026

commands.name: show ip route
commands.desc: Shows the IPv4 routing table including connected, local, static, and dynamic routes. Use it to verify a route to a remote network exists.
commands.sample:
C    192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
L    192.168.1.1/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
S    10.0.0.0/8 [1/0] via 192.168.2.1

commands.name: show interfaces
commands.desc: Shows detailed statistics for interfaces: line/keepalive state, input/output errors, collisions, and speed/duplex. Use it to spot duplex mismatch and interface errors.
commands.sample:
GigabitEthernet0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  Full-duplex, 100Mb/s
  5 input errors, 0 CRC, 0 collisions

commands.name: show running-config
commands.desc: Displays the current active configuration stored in RAM. Use it to inspect the applied configuration before saving it.
commands.sample:
hostname R1
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown

commands.name: debug ip icmp
commands.desc: Logs ICMP packets in real time to see if pings arrive and are answered. Useful to confirm traffic reaches a router.
commands.sample: ICMP: echo reply sent, src 192.168.1.1, dst 192.168.1.10

commands.name: terminal monitor
commands.desc: Displays debugging and log messages on the current console/vty session instead of only the console. Run it before debugging from a remote session.
commands.sample: (no output; enables console logging for this session)

commands.name: undebug all
commands.desc: Disables all debugging. Debugging is processor-intensive and should always be turned off after troubleshooting.
commands.sample: All possible debugging has been turned off

commands.name: no shutdown
commands.desc: Interface configuration command that enables an interface (administratively up). The inverse, shutdown, disables it.
commands.sample: R1(config-if)# no shutdown

commands.name: ip address
commands.desc: Interface configuration command that assigns an IPv4 address and subnet mask to an interface. Use no shutdown if the interface was administratively shut down (interfaces are up by default).

commands.name: ipv6 address
commands.desc: Interface configuration command that assigns a static IPv6 GUA (or ULA) to an interface.
commands.sample: R1(config-if)# ipv6 address 2001:DB8:ACAD:1::1/64

commands.name: ipv6 unicast-routing
commands.desc: Global configuration command that enables IPv6 routing on a router so it can forward IPv6 packets and send Router Advertisements.
commands.sample: R1(config)# ipv6 unicast-routing

commands.name: hostname
commands.desc: Global configuration command that sets the device name shown in the prompt.
commands.sample: R1(config)# hostname R1

commands.name: enable
commands.desc: Moves from user EXEC mode to privileged EXEC mode (if a password is set, it is requested). Needed before show/configure commands that require privilege.
commands.sample:
Switch> enable
Switch#

commands.name: configure terminal
commands.desc: Moves from privileged EXEC mode to global configuration mode for changing the running configuration.
commands.sample:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)#

commands.name: copy running-config startup-config
commands.desc: Saves the active running configuration to NVRAM (startup-config) so it survives a reload. Also abbreviated as copy run start.
commands.sample:
R1# copy running-config startup-config
[OK]

commands.name: netsh interface ipv6 set address
commands.desc: Assigns a static IPv6 address to a Windows interface (equivalent of static GUA config).
commands.sample: C:\> netsh interface ipv6 set address "Ethernet0" 2001:db8:acad:1::10/64

commands.name: netsh interface ipv6 show address
commands.desc: Displays IPv6 addresses assigned to Windows interfaces, including link-local and global addresses.
commands.sample:
Interface 3: Ethernet0
  Address 2001:db8:acad:1::10
  Address fe80::a00:27ff:fe11:2233

commands.name: show ipv6 route
commands.desc: Displays the IPv6 routing table including connected, local, static, and dynamic routes.
commands.sample:
IPv6 Routing Table - 3 entries
C  2001:DB8:ACAD:1::/64 [0/0] via GigabitEthernet0/0, directly connected
L  2001:DB8:ACAD:1::1/128 [0/0] via GigabitEthernet0/0, receive

commands.name: show ipv6 neighbors
commands.desc: Displays the IPv6 neighbor cache mapping IPv6 addresses to MAC addresses (the IPv6 equivalent of the ARP table).
commands.sample:
Interface    IPv6 Address       Age Link-layer Addr
Gig0/0      2001:DB8:ACAD:1::10 1  0050.7966.0400

commands.name: ping ipv6
commands.desc: Tests IPv6 reachability using ICMPv6 Echo Request/Echo Reply. On Cisco IOS, ping ipv6 addresses an IPv6 destination; on Linux use ping -6.
commands.sample:
R1# ping ipv6 2001:DB8:ACAD:1::10
Sending 5, 100-byte ICMP Echos to 2001:DB8:ACAD:1::10, timeout is 2 seconds:
!!!!!
Success rate is 100 percent (5/5), round-trip min/avg/max = 1/2/4 ms
(On Linux: ping -6 2001:db8:acad:1::10 prints '64 bytes from ... icmp_seq=...')
